title: Traverse the Compression Tree with DFS
real_world_story: A compression system needs to inspect every branch of its binary encoding tree to analyze the complete structure of encoded data.

real_world_connection.input_represents: A binary encoding tree stored in level-order
real_world_connection.target_represents: The order in which nodes are visited while exploring each branch deeply
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Using Depth First Search to explore a tree branch before moving to the next branch

problem_statement: Given a binary tree represented in level-order where -1 represents a missing node, print all existing node values using a preorder Depth First Search traversal.
task: Traverse the binary tree using DFS in preorder and print the values in the order they are visited.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N, the number of positions in the level-order representation. The second line contains N space-separated integers. A value of -1 represents a missing node.
output_format: Print the existing node values in preorder DFS order separated by spaces. If the tree is empty, print -1.
constraints: The first position represents the root

examples.explanation: Preorder DFS visits the root first, then completely explores the left subtree before visiting the right subtree.
DFS explores the left branch deeply before moving to the right branch.

expected_algorithm.name: Tree DFS
expected_algorithm.reason: Depth First Search explores one branch of the binary tree completely before moving to another branch, making it useful for examining hierarchical encoding structures.

hint: Process the current node before its children.
Recursively or iteratively visit the left subtree.
After completing the left subtree, visit the right subtree.
real_world_takeaway: DFS helps compression systems inspect complete branches of hierarchical encoding structures and analyze how encoded information is organized along individual paths.
